newsitem.title: USA: CBOE to restrict Centennial CTN options trade.
newsitem.headline: CBOE to restrict Centennial CTN options trade.

text.p: The Chicago Board Options Exchange said Wednesday that if and when it re-opens trading on options on shares of Centennial Technologies Inc, it would restrict trade to closing transactions.

The exchange said in a statement that only closing transactions would be allowed in any series of Centennial options except for opening transactions by market makers executed to accommodate closing trades of other participants.

"Members shall be permitted to effect opening transactions in CTN options only in order to facilitate closing transactions of customers, in the event that members of the trading crowd do not elect to accommodate a customer's closing order," the CBOE said.
It added that no determination had yet been made to restrict exercises in Centennial options.
The New York Stock Exchange halted trading in Centennial shares late Tuesday, and the halt remained in effect Wednesday. The shares last closed at 14-3/4.
The American Stock Exchange said it would resume Centennial options trading immediately after the underlying shares are re-opened and also said it would limit trading to closing transactions.
On February 18, the NYSE said it would suspend trading of Centennial's common stock on March 3 and would afterwards apply to federal regulators to delist it.
The CBOE said Wednesday it had been notified that the NYSE would suspend trading in Centennial common stock as of the close of trading on February 28.
